newsitem.title: USA: USWC products ease amid neutral APIs, thin news.
newsitem.headline: USWC products ease amid neutral APIs, thin news.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products eased in light Tuesday trade, as neutral inventory data and a lack of refinery incidents dulled interest in spot trade, brokers said.
"Everyone sees the market the same way and there are no buyers," said one California-based broker.

West Coast gasoline stocks gained a slight 98,000 barrels as of March 28, while refinery utilization was nearly unchanged at 89.8 percent of capacity, according to a weekly report published by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
ARCO Tuesday denied rumors its Los Angeles-area refinery was unable to make diesel fuel, curbing morning gains.
CARB diesel in L.A. fell one cent Tuesday to 77.50/78.50 after firming earlier amid rumors that ARCO lost use of its hydrocracker, a unit which helps to make diesel.
In gasoline markets, prices have lost support since Tosco and their oil workers on Saturday agreed to a labor contract, ending the threat of strike at four California refineries.

CARB gasoline in Los Angeles shed a 1.50 cent from Monday, with traders talking the grade between 81.50 and 82.50 cents a gallon. San Francisco ranged a half-cent under L.A., losing 2.00 cents since Monday.
